meta.description: Gold labels for the 10 appendix tickets in data/sample_tickets.json. Tickets themselves live there; this file adds the labels (join on id).

category.technical: bugs, errors, outages, API failures, broken features
category.account: login, password, email changes, account access
category.other: everything else, feature requests, unclear messages

priority.high: urgent, production blocking: outage/errors hitting production or many users, or explicit urgency with material impact
priority.medium: normal priority: default; routine requests and single-user issues
priority.low: nice to have, not urgent: explicitly non-urgent, cosmetic, informational

meta.provenance: Categories for all 10 tickets are pinned by the README's zero-shot agreement table (8/10, misses t-1006/t-1008) and the QA report's FakeLLM table (9/10, miss t-1009). Priorities are pinned by tests/test_classification.py for t-1003 (high) and t-1006 (low) only; the rest are rubric-derived and marked asserted:false in the notes.
meta.notes: Judgement calls worth a human look: t-1007 (accountant deadline but routine fix -> medium), t-1008 (nonsense message, no urgency marker -> default medium), t-1010 (repeated failure but single-user, not production -> medium), t-1005 (subject says URGENT but that text is the injection payload; the real question is routine -> medium).
